question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{a}^{2}-2ab+{b}^{2}=(a-b)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
25{x}^{2}-20x+4.
$$

First, we write both the quadratic term and the constant term as perfect squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5x)^{2}-20x+(2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5x)^{2}-2(10x)+(2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we write the middle parentheses $(10x)$ as a product of $5x$ and $2:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(5x)^{2}-2(5x\cdot 2)+(2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=5x$ and $b=2.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}(5x-2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
